- Location of maximal tenderness (e.g., tibial tubercle vs. patellar tendon vs. medial joint line).  
- Physical exam findings: active/passive range of motion, presence of resisted extension pain, patellar grind, tibial tubercle tenderness or enlargement.  
- Whether pain is reproducible with resisted knee extension (key for OSD).  
- Radiographic findings (X-ray may show fragmentation or ossicle at tibial tubercle — though early OSD can be radiographically normal).

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Osgood-Schlatter disease
